text: Increased disclosure obligations let so-called pilot fish emulate hedge funds' investment strategies and positions, which makes those positions more expensive to build and strips systematic bargaining strength from the negotiation process.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Hedge Funds’ Systemic Risk Disclosures in Bankruptcy (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2348463

isBasedOn.name: Hedge Funds’ Systemic Risk Disclosures in Bankruptcy

abstract: disclosure obligations, "pilot fish" can increasingly emulate investment strategies and positions. As a result, investment positions can become more expensive and systematic bargaining strength is removed from the negotiation process.

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: markets where competitors can observe and copy disclosed positions
